one_liner: Prototype non-backtracking JIT regex compiler for x86-64 that beats RE2 and grep on throughput, unmaintained since 2015.
what_it_does: Rejit is a C++ library that JIT-compiles regular expressions to native x86-64 code for fast matching and replacing over in-memory text. The API is a `Regej` class plus free functions (`MatchFull`, `MatchAnywhere`, `MatchFirst`, `MatchAll`, `MatchAllCount`, `ReplaceFirst`, `ReplaceAll`) taking a `const char*` pattern and `std::string`/`char*`+size text, returning `bool` or a `Match{begin,end}` pointer pair. It is not a drop-in for RE2: the API shape differs and there is no capture-group extraction. The repo also ships `jrep`, a `grep`-like CLI sample built on rejit.
how_it_is_fast: Each regex is JIT-compiled at runtime into native x86-64 machine code using a V8-derived assembler/codegen (src/x64/assembler-x64.*), avoiding backtracking entirely. Matching uses SIMD to test up to 4 characters per instruction (kMaxParallelChars=4 in src/cpu.h, requires SSE4.2, disable with simd:off) and a 'fast forward' skip-ahead mechanism that jumps past non-matching regions instead of scanning byte by byte. The multi-threaded benchmark samples (jrep -R, regexdna-multithread.cc) add throughput by splitting input across threads manually.
when_to_use: Bulk, offline x86_64 Linux/macOS text-scanning jobs where you can vendor a small unmaintained C++11 GPLv3 static lib for extra single-machine regex throughput on large inputs (tens of MB+)
Simple find/match/replace patterns that don't need capture groups, back-references, word boundaries, Unicode/UTF-8, or POSIX BRE syntax
You already split work across threads yourself (as jrep and the DNA benchmark samples do) and want a non-backtracking engine per thread
Studying or extending a small, readable non-backtracking SIMD regex JIT implementation
GPL-3.0 licensing is acceptable in your project
when_not_to_use: You need capture/submatch extraction: issue #6 'Support submatches extraction' has been open since 2014 and unresolved; Match only exposes begin/end of the whole match
You need word boundaries (\b), back-references, Unicode/UTF-8 encoding, or POSIX BRE syntax: all are open, unimplemented feature requests (issues #1, #3, #5, #7)
Non-x86_64 targets: issue #10 'Support other architectures' is open and unaddressed; SConstruct only builds arch:x64

Production or long-lived use: no commits since April 2015, and the SConstruct build script itself prints a warning that 'top-of-tree is not maintained any more, and contains some bugs. In particular, some regular expressions are incorrectly evaluated,' pointing to an apparently-unfinished successor (arames/regit)
You need permissive licensing or static linking into a non-GPL product: license is GPL-3.0

integration.dependencies: none for the core library at build time (SCons is the build tool, not a runtime dependency); the benchmark harness separately depends on RE2, V8, and PCRE for comparison only
integration.min_toolchain: C++11 (SConstruct sets CXXFLAGS -std=c++11); specific compiler/version not stated; built with SCons
integration.platforms: x86_64 only, SIMD path assumes SSE4.2 (kMaxParallelChars=4 in src/cpu.h); SConstruct has Linux and macOS build configs; other architectures are an open, unimplemented issue (#10)
integration.thread_safety: not documented for the Regej class; the multi-threaded sample programs (jrep, regexdna-multithread.cc) achieve concurrency by giving each thread its own Regej instance and text range
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — explain: C++-only API (no C bindings; issue #11 'C support' is open), and there is no RE2-style capture-group API, so call sites need to be rewritten, not just relinked

gotchas: The project's own SConstruct prints a build-time warning: 'top-of-tree is not maintained any more, and contains some bugs. In particular, some regular expressions are incorrectly evaluated.'
No capture-group/submatch API — Match exposes only begin/end of the whole match (issue #6 open since 2014)
x86_64-only; the SIMD fast path assumes SSE4.2 and can be turned off at build time with simd:off
The public header include/rejit.h has `using namespace std;` at file scope, which can leak std:: names into including translation units
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick rejit over BLARE or re2jit only if you want a from-scratch, dependency-free non-backtracking JIT engine to study or extend and don't need RE2-compatible behavior; BLARE reports broader RE2/PCRE2/Boost comparisons and re2jit stays API-compatible with RE2 (it falls back to RE2 for cases it doesn't optimize), while rejit offers neither RE2 API compatibility nor capture groups.
verified_claims_summary: First-party README benchmarks on an Intel Core i5-2400 (quad-core, SSE4.2, Fedora 17, RE2 commit aa957b5e3374 from ~2013): multi-threaded Rejit vs. the Benchmarks Game RE2 regex-dna program is 1.68x-2.1x faster in real time across 500KB-500MB inputs, and Rejit-powered jrep is 1.68x faster than GNU grep 2.14 on `grep -R` over the Linux 3.10.6 source tree (0.370s vs 0.622s real); the compiler and optimization flags actually used for these runs are not stated.
status_note: Abandoned since its last commit in April 2015; GPL-3.0, C++11, and small enough (~20 source files) to vendor as a source-drop, but the build script itself warns of known incorrect-match bugs and never reached a maintained successor.
